subject: mean vs expected group size in MRDS

messages.author: 8ee41a379d8797bf
messages.subject: mean vs expected group size in MRDS
parts:
HI,

we talked recently about the issue of mean and expected cluster size. My question now is, given that MRDS is supposed to NOT deal with a regression line to get an expected cluster size (as is one of the options in MCDS), BUT in the results section it provides the mean cluster size and the "expected" cluster size (which is actually different from that estimated front he regression line in MCDS). ANd double checking the abundance estimates, these are calculated using this "expected" cluster size in MRDS, not the mean. 
So my question is, if it is not through a regression line, what is the "expected" cluster size shown in the results section of MRDS?

Many thanks
Ana Canadas

messages.author: 7482eee8d2863d12
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] mean vs expected group size in MRDS
parts:
Hi Ana, (list)

Summary: expected cluster size is estimated number of individuals
divided by estimated number of clusters.

Longer answer - first some notation:
Let i = 1, ... , n index the observations; let z_i be the vector of
detection function covariates for observation i, which might include s_i
the observed cluster size for that observation. Assume we've fitted a
detection function using MCDS or MRDS and that \hat{p}(z_i) is the
estimated detection probability for the ith observation given its
covariates z_i.

Then, the estimated number of individuals in the covered area (i.e., the
transects) is given by the Horvitz-Thompson-like estimator

\hat{N} = sum_{i=1}^n \frac{s_i}{\hat{p}(z_i)}

(in case you're not used to LaTeX notation that's the sum over all
observations of s_i divided by \hat{p}(z_i)).

The estimated number of clusters is given by

\hat{N_c} = sum_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{\hat{p}(z_i)}

(similar but the sum of 1 divided by \hat{p}(z_i)).

The estimated expected cluster size is simply \hat{N_c} divided by \hat{N}.

So, it's not really that the abundance estimates are calculated using
the expected cluster size - instead it's the expected cluster size is
calculated using the abundance estimates!

Hope this helps! Len

Cheers
Ana

messages.author: 7482eee8d2863d12
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] mean vs expected group size in MRDS
parts:
Nope, it's not the same as using mean group size.

(In formulae:
\hat{N} = sum_{i=1}^n \frac{s_i}{\hat{p}(z_i)}

i.e., the sum of s_i/p(z_i), summed over all observed animals

is not the same as

\hat{N} = \frac{sum_{i=1}^n s_i}{n} \frac{1}{\hat{p}(z_i)}

i.e., mean group size times sum of 1/p(z_i) summed over all observed animals

unless all of the z_i's are the same - i.e., no covariates.)

You can think of it as using an estimate of the population mean group
size, rather than the observed mean group size.

Best, Len
